title: Chapter 88 — Schools and Schoolmasters
paragraphs: The previous chapter gave an account of an immense body or herd of sperm whales, and there was also given the probable cause behind those vast gatherings.

Now, though such great bodies are at times encountered, as has been seen, even today small separate bands are occasionally observed, ranging from twenty to fifty individuals each. Such bands are known as schools. They are generally of two sorts: those composed almost entirely of females, and those mustering none but young, vigorous males — or bulls, as they are familiarly called.

In gallant attendance upon the school of females, you invariably see a male of full-grown size, but not old, who upon any alarm shows his chivalry by falling to the rear and covering the flight of his ladies. In truth, this gentleman is a luxurious sultan, swimming about the watery world, surrounded by all the comforts and pleasures of the harem. The contrast between this sultan and his consorts is striking, because while he is always of the largest proportions, the ladies, even at full growth, are not more than one-third the bulk of an average-sized male. They are comparatively delicate, indeed — I daresay not exceeding half a dozen yards around the waist. Nevertheless, it cannot be denied that on the whole they are hereditarily entitled to plumpness.

It is very curious to watch this harem and its lord in their indolent wanderings. Like fashionable society, they are forever on the move in leisurely search of variety. You meet them on the equator in time for the full bloom of the feeding season, having just returned perhaps from spending the summer in the northern seas, and so cheating summer of all its unpleasant weariness and warmth. By the time they have lounged up and down the equatorial promenade awhile, they start for the eastern waters in anticipation of the cool season there, and so evade the other excessive temperature of the year.

When serenely traveling on one of these journeys, if any strange suspicious sights are seen, the lord whale keeps a wary eye on his interesting family. Should any rudely bold young Leviathan happen that way and presume to draw confidentially close to one of the ladies — with what prodigious fury the lord assails him and chases him away! High times indeed, if unprincipled young rakes like him are to be permitted to invade the sanctity of domestic bliss. Though do what the lord will, he cannot keep the most notorious seducer out of his bed, for alas, all fish bed in common. As on shore, the ladies often cause the most terrible duels among their rival admirers. Just so with the whales, who sometimes come to deadly battle, and all for love. They fence with their long lower jaws, sometimes locking them together and striving for supremacy like elks that warring interweave their antlers. Not a few are captured bearing the deep scars of these encounters: furrowed heads, broken teeth, scalloped fins, and in some instances wrenched and dislocated mouths.

But suppose the invader of domestic bliss takes himself away at the first rush of the harem's lord. Then it is very amusing to watch that lord. Gently he insinuates his vast bulk among them again and revels there awhile, still in tantalizing proximity to young Lothario, like pious Solomon devoutly worshipping among his thousand concubines. Granting other whales to be in sight, the fishermen will seldom give chase to one of these grand sultans, for these grand sultans are too lavish with their strength, and hence their oil-yield is small. As for the sons and daughters they beget, those sons and daughters must take care of themselves — at least with only the mother's help. For like certain other roving lovers that might be named, the lord whale has no taste for the nursery, however much for the bower. And so, being a great traveler, he leaves his anonymous babies all over the world, every baby an exotic. In good time, nevertheless, as the ardor of youth declines — as years and gloom increase, as reflection lends her solemn pauses — in short, as a general weariness overtakes the sated sultan, a love of ease and virtue replaces the love of maidens. Our lord enters upon the impotent, repentant, lecturing stage of life, forswears and disbands the harem, and grown to an exemplary, sulky old soul, goes about all alone among the meridians and parallels saying his prayers and warning each young Leviathan from his amorous errors.

Now, as the harem of whales is called by the fishermen a school, so is the lord and master of that school technically known as the schoolmaster. It is therefore not in strict character — however admirably satirical — that after going to school himself, he should then go abroad teaching not what he learned there but the folly of it. His title of schoolmaster would very naturally seem derived from the name of the harem itself. But some have guessed that the man who first gave this name to this sort of sultan whale must have read the memoirs of Vidocq, and informed himself what sort of country schoolmaster that famous Frenchman was in his younger days, and what was the nature of those secret lessons he taught some of his pupils.

The same seclusion and isolation to which the schoolmaster whale retreats in his advancing years is true of all aged sperm whales. Almost universally, a lone whale — as a solitary Leviathan is called — proves to be an ancient one. Like the venerable moss-bearded Daniel Boone, he will have no one near him but Nature herself. And her he takes to wife in the wilderness of waters — and the best of wives she is, though she keeps so many moody secrets.

The schools composed of nothing but young, vigorous males, previously mentioned, offer a strong contrast to the harem schools. For while those female whales are characteristically timid, the young males — or forty-barrel-bulls, as they call them — are by far the most combative of all Leviathans and proverbially the most dangerous to encounter, excepting those wondrous gray-headed, grizzled whales sometimes met, who will fight you like grim fiends aggravated by gout.

The forty-barrel-bull schools are larger than the harem schools. Like a mob of young college men, they are full of fight, fun, and mischief, tumbling round the world at such a reckless, rollicking rate that no prudent insurance man would cover them any more than he would a riotous student at Yale or Harvard. They soon outgrow this wildness, though, and when about three-quarters grown, they break up and separately go about in quest of settlements — that is, harems.

Another difference between the male and female schools is still more characteristic of the sexes. Say you strike a forty-barrel-bull: poor devil! All his comrades abandon him. But strike a member of the harem school, and her companions swim around her with every sign of concern, sometimes lingering so near and so long as to fall prey themselves.
